summary: coeff() bounds the angle type range with atom->ndihedraltypes instead of atom->nangletypes, so coefficients are uploaded for the wrong number of types (out-of-bounds writes or silently missing types).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:300-311: `int ilo,ihi;` / `utils::bounds(FLERR,arg[0],1,atom->ndihedraltypes,ilo,ihi,error);` / `for (int i = ilo; i <= ihi; i++) { k_nterms.view_host()[i] = nterms[i]; ... }`. The CPU base uses the angle type count: src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_gaussian.cpp:208-209: `int ilo, ihi;` / `utils::bounds(FLERR, arg[0], 1, atom->nangletypes, ilo, ihi, error);`. Every sibling in this group also uses nangletypes, e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_charmm_kokkos.cpp:284 `utils::bounds(FLERR,arg[0],1,atom->nangletypes,ilo,ihi,error);`. The dual views being indexed are sized nangletypes+1 (src/KOKKOS/angle_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:65-71, 282-283).
failure_scenario: Any angle-only system (no dihedrals, atom->ndihedraltypes == 0): `angle_style gaussian/kk` + `angle_coeff 1 300.0 2 ...` aborts with the bogus error 'Numeric index 1 is out of bounds (1-0)'. If ndihedraltypes > nangletypes, `angle_coeff * ...` writes k_nterms/k_angle_temperature/k_alpha/k_width/k_theta0 host mirrors past index nangletypes -> heap corruption. If 0 < ndihedraltypes < nangletypes, `angle_coeff * ...` uploads only the first ndihedraltypes types; the remaining types keep nterms==0 on the device, so their Gaussian sum is 0 -> log(0) energy and 0/0 forces.
suggested_fix: Change `atom->ndihedraltypes` to `atom->nangletypes` on line 301 to match AngleGaussian::coeff.

summary: The sin(theta) floor used to regularize the 1/s force prefactor is 1e-12 instead of the base class's SMALL = 0.001, so near-collinear angles get forces up to ~1e9 times larger than the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_cosine_shift_exp_kokkos.cpp:188-189: `KK_FLOAT s = Kokkos::sqrt(static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1.0) - c*c);` / `if (s < static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1e-12)) s = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1e-12);`, and s is then divided into the force at lines 204 (`ff = 0.25*uumin*cssmscc*(2.0+aa*cccpsss)/s;`) and 209 (`ff = 0.5*aa*d_opt1[type]*exp2*cssmscc/s;`). The CPU base uses 0.001: src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_cosine_shift_exp.cpp:35 `static constexpr double SMALL = 0.001;` and :118-120 `s = sqrt(1.0 - c*c);` / `if (s < SMALL) s = SMALL;` with the same `ff=...cssmscc/s` at :130 and :138. Every other Kokkos angle style in this group keeps the base value (e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_cosine_shift_kokkos.cpp:34,188 use SMALL=0.001; angle_charmm_kokkos.cpp:34,198; angle_cross_kokkos.cpp:30,173).
failure_scenario: angle_style cosine/shift/exp/kk with an angle driven close to 0 or 180 degrees (sin(theta) < 1e-3, i.e. within ~0.06 deg of collinear) while theta0 is not collinear: the CPU caps the prefactor at ff <= C/0.001, the KOKKOS kernel allows ff up to C/1e-12, giving forces ~1e9x larger -> 'lost atoms'/blown-up trajectory where the CPU run is stable, and a force/energy mismatch in force-style regression tests.
suggested_fix: Add `static constexpr double SMALL = 0.001;` at the top of the file (as in the sibling styles) and use it for the clamp so the /kk variant reproduces AngleCosineShiftExp exactly.

summary: The sum_g_i underflow guard uses SMALLG = 2.3e-308 cast to KK_FLOAT, which becomes exactly 0.0f in single/mixed-precision KOKKOS builds and therefore never fires.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_gaussian_kokkos.cpp:31 `static constexpr double SMALLG = 2.3e-308;` and :221-223 `// avoid overflow` / `if (sum_g_i < sum_numerator * static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALLG))` / `sum_g_i = sum_numerator * static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALLG);`. KK_FLOAT is `float` for LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE and LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_DOUBLE (src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:399-408), and static_cast<float>(2.3e-308) underflows to 0.0f, so the test degenerates to `if (sum_g_i < 0.0f)`. sum_g_i is then used at :228 `eangle = -kbt * Kokkos::log(sum_g_i);` and :230 `a = -4.0*kbt*(sum_numerator/sum_g_i)*s;`. The CPU base performs the identical guard in double: src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_gaussian.cpp:32 and :135-136.
failure_scenario: Build with -DLMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE (or SINGLE_DOUBLE) and run angle_style gaussian/kk with an angle far from every theta0 (all exponents very negative): every g_i underflows, sum_g_i == 0.0f, the guard does not fire, log(0) gives -inf energy and sum_numerator/sum_g_i gives inf/NaN forces -> NaN trajectory. The double-precision default build is unaffected.
suggested_fix: Evaluate the guard in double (or use a KK_FLOAT-appropriate floor such as Kokkos::Experimental::norm_min_v<KK_FLOAT> / std::numeric_limits<KK_FLOAT>::min()) instead of casting a double-denormal constant to KK_FLOAT.

summary: The degenerate-geometry guards compare against SMALL*SMALL with SMALL = 1.0e-100, which underflows to 0 when KK_FLOAT is float, so the zero-length checks that the CPU style relies on become inert.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_dipole_kokkos.cpp:31 `static constexpr double SMALL = 1.0e-100;`, :154-155 `const KK_FLOAT r2 = delx*delx + dely*dely + delz*delz;` / `if (r2 < static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALL)*static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALL)) return;` and :181-183 `const KK_FLOAT len2 = fx*fx + fy*fy + fz*fz;` / `if (len2 < static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALL)*static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(SMALL)) return;`. With KK_FLOAT = float (src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:399-408, LMP_KOKKOS_SINGLE_SINGLE / SINGLE_DOUBLE) static_cast<float>(1.0e-100) is 0.0f, so both tests become `< 0.0f` and never trigger. The CPU base tests the un-squared quantity in double: src/DIPOLE/angle_dipole.cpp:35 `static constexpr double SMALL = 1.0e-100;`, :94-95 `r = sqrt(...); if (r < SMALL) continue;` and :120-121 `len = sqrt(fx*fx+fy*fy+fz*fz); if (len < SMALL) continue;`.
failure_scenario: Single/mixed-precision KOKKOS build, angle_style dipole/kk, with a dipole atom coincident with its reference atom (r == 0) or a dipole exactly parallel to the bond vector (delT == 0 so fx=fy=fz=0): the CPU skips the angle, the /kk kernel divides by rmu == 0 or by sqrt(len2) == 0 and writes inf/NaN into torque and f.
suggested_fix: Do the comparison in double (compare `static_cast<double>(r2) < SMALL*SMALL`) or replace 1.0e-100 with a floor representable in KK_FLOAT.

summary: The device kernel calls the host <cmath> function fmod() instead of Kokkos::fmod(), violating the KOKKOS rule that device kernels use Kokkos:: math functions.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_fourier_simple_kokkos.cpp:186-187 inside the KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION operator(): `sgn = (fmod(static_cast<double>(d_N[type]), 2.0) == 0.0) ? static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(-1.0) : static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1.0);`. Every other math call in the same kernel is namespace-qualified (`Kokkos::sqrt` :154, `Kokkos::acos` :169, `Kokkos::cos` :171, `Kokkos::sin` :178, `Kokkos::fabs` :177). .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: 'Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels (Kokkos::sqrt, Kokkos::exp, Kokkos::pow, Kokkos::log, ...), never std:: -- std::pow and friends fail to compile for GPU targets.' The CPU original is src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_fourier_simple.cpp:132 `sgn = (fmod(N[type], 2.0) == 0.0) ? -1.0 : 1.0;`.
failure_scenario: Backends that do not inject a __device__ overload of the unqualified ::fmod (SYCL/OpenMPTarget, or a build where <cmath> pulls in only the host overload) fail to compile angle_fourier_simple_kokkos.cpp. Where it does compile it forces a double-precision fmod inside an otherwise single-precision kernel.

summary: 13 of the 16 angle KOKKOS styles in this group have no `action` lines in src/KOKKOS/Install.sh, contrary to KOKKOS rule 5.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/Install.sh:37-50 lists only angle_charmm, angle_class2, angle_cosine, angle_table, angle_harmonic, angle_hybrid and angle_spica. Missing: angle_class2_p6_kokkos.{cpp,h} (base src/MOFFF/angle_class2_p6.cpp), angle_class2xe_kokkos.{cpp,h} (src/CLASS2/angle_class2xe.cpp), angle_cosine_delta_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_periodic_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_shift_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_shift_exp_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_squared_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cosine_squared_restricted_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_cross_kokkos.{cpp,h} (src/YAFF/angle_cross.cpp), angle_dipole_kokkos.{cpp,h} (src/DIPOLE/angle_dipole.cpp), angle_fourier_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_fourier_simple_kokkos.{cpp,h}, angle_gaussian_kokkos.{cpp,h}. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 5 requires an action line per new file, with the base file name as second argument when the base lives in an optional package.
failure_scenario: No build breakage today: KOKKOS's action() only does `rm -f ../$1` (install mode is refused outright at Install.sh:216) and CMake finds the files through RegisterStylesExt (cmake/Modules/Packages/KOKKOS.cmake:304). The consequence is that `make no-kokkos`/`make purge` will not remove stale src/ copies of these files left over from an older tree, and the file list drifts out of sync with the documented convention.
suggested_fix: Add the 26 missing `action <file> <base file>` lines to src/KOKKOS/Install.sh in alphabetical order alongside the existing angle_* entries.

summary: Four setflag dual views are allocated as floating-point arrays, filled, and synced to the device on every compute() call, but no kernel ever reads them.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_class2_kokkos.cpp:100-103 syncs `k_setflag`, `k_setflag_a`, `k_setflag_bb`, `k_setflag_ba` each timestep; :339-342 allocates them as `DAT::tdual_kkfloat_1d` (integer flags stored as KK_FLOAT); :356-359 and :447-450 assign d_setflag/d_setflag_a/d_setflag_bb/d_setflag_ba; :386-389 and :465-468 fill them. The device views d_setflag* appear nowhere in operator() (:162-308) or ev_tally (:498-603), and the CPU base never reads setflag in compute() either (src/CLASS2/angle_class2.cpp:76-239).
failure_scenario: No wrong results; 4 extra device allocations of (nangletypes+1) KK_FLOATs plus 4 no-op DualView syncs per timestep, and integer flags stored in a float view (silently lossy above 2^24 - irrelevant for 0/1 but wrong typing).
suggested_fix: Delete k_setflag/k_setflag_a/k_setflag_bb/k_setflag_ba, their d_* views, and the corresponding allocate/coeff/read_restart/compute lines.

summary: `d_ba_r2 = k_ba_r2.template view<DeviceType>();` is duplicated in both allocate() and read_restart(), a copy-paste leftover that likely masks a missing assignment.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_class2_kokkos.cpp:354-356: `d_ba_r1 = k_ba_r1.template view<DeviceType>();` / `d_ba_r2 = k_ba_r2.template view<DeviceType>();` / `d_ba_r2 = k_ba_r2.template view<DeviceType>();` and the identical pair at :445-446. All other d_* views are assigned exactly once.
failure_scenario: Harmless as written (the second assignment is idempotent), but it is the classic shape of a dropped `d_theta0`/`d_ba_k2` assignment and confuses future edits.
suggested_fix: Delete the duplicate line at 355 and at 446.

summary: The per-atom energy/virial arrays are registered with the memory tag 'improper:eatom'/'improper:vatom' inside an angle style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_charmm_kokkos.cpp:77 `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom,maxeatom,"improper:eatom");` and :84 `memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_vatom,vatom,maxvatom,"improper:vatom");`. Every sibling uses the correct tag, e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_class2_kokkos.cpp:76,81 `"angle:eatom"`, `"angle:vatom"`, matching the CPU base src/angle.cpp:137,144 ("angle:eatom", "angle:vatom").
failure_scenario: No numerical effect; the allocation is attributed to 'improper' in `info memory` / memory-usage output, which misleads anyone tracking KOKKOS memory.

summary: k_eatom/k_vatom are destroyed and reallocated on every timestep on which per-atom energy/virial is requested, instead of the reuse-and-zero pattern used by the other 13 styles in this group.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_charmm_kokkos.cpp:74-87 (with the commented-out size check `//if(k_eatom.extent(0)<maxeatom) { // won't work without adding zero functor`), src/KOKKOS/angle_class2_kokkos.cpp:74-83 and src/KOKKOS/angle_cosine_kokkos.cpp:72-81 do an unconditional `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(...)` + `memoryKK->create_kokkos(...)`. The other styles solved the zeroing problem and reuse the buffer, e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_class2xe_kokkos.cpp:74-80: `if ((int)k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) { destroy; create; d_eatom = ...; } else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);`.
failure_scenario: No wrong results. With `compute pe/atom` or `compute stress/atom` active every output step triggers a device free+malloc of nmax (and 6*nmax) elements per angle style; on GPUs this serializes the step and can dominate the angle cost.
suggested_fix: Adopt the extent-check + Kokkos::deep_copy(...,0.0) pattern already used by angle_class2xe_kokkos.cpp and the other 13 styles in this group.

summary: The energy is rebuilt as cos(theta)cos(theta0)+sin(theta)sin(theta0) using the SMALL-clamped sine, so it differs from the base class's exact cos(theta-theta0) for near-collinear angles.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_cosine_delta_kokkos.cpp:189-201: `KK_FLOAT s = Kokkos::sqrt(1.0 - c*c);` / `if (s < SMALL) s = SMALL;` / `const KK_FLOAT cot = c/s;` / ... / `const KK_FLOAT dcostheta = c*c0 + s*s0;` / `const KK_FLOAT tk = d_k[type] * (1.0 - dcostheta);` / `if (eflag) eangle = tk;`. The CPU base clamps s only for the cot term and computes the energy from the unclamped angle: src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_cosine_delta.cpp:87-98: `theta = acos(c);` / `s = sqrt(1.0 - c*c); if (s < SMALL) s = SMALL; cot = c/s;` / `dtheta = theta - theta0[type]; dcostheta = cos(dtheta); tk = k[type] * (1.0-dcostheta);`. SMALL is 0.001 in both (kokkos line 34, base line 35). The force terms a11/a12/a22/b11/b12/b22 are identical, so only the energy diverges.
failure_scenario: angle_style cosine/delta/kk with an angle within ~0.06 deg of 0 or 180 degrees: the /kk energy is off by k*(0.001 - sin(theta))*sin(theta0), i.e. up to 1e-3*k per angle, versus the CPU value. Shows up as a small but systematic energy mismatch in force-style regression tests for collapsed/linear angles.
suggested_fix: Compute the energy from the unclamped sine (keep a separate clamped copy for cot), or use Kokkos::cos(Kokkos::acos(c) - theta0) as the base does.
